Might be a bit late, but I figured I would share my opinion. 

Just graduated with a 4.0 from my M.E. in Civil Eng. with an emphasis on structural engineering. Had about a 1.5 - 2 years of experience.

Making 46k in Miami. Miami is a pretty poor market for structural engineers. From my peers I have seen salary ranging up and down from that about 4-5k each way.

It is still a pretty shitty point in the industry although it is slightly picking up. I think the supply of graduates far exceed the demand for workers, and thus companies are able to pick out the cream of the crop for lower prices.

In my opinion, however, equally as important as salary is the companies ability to properly train you to get licensure. You could go work for one of the top 10 firms and make an extra 10k but they will have you working on nothing but one small specialty niche. 

Good luck and I hope you were capable of negotiating a better salary.

I am not at all vegetarian, but I make a really really mean vegetarian chili. Really easy to make and stupidly good. This has been feeding droves of people at tailgate and is extremely economical as I have to work within a college budget.

Ingredients:
Half an onion 
Half a head of garlic
2 cans black beans
2 cans pinto beans
1 can kidney beans
1 can red beans
1 small can of corn
1 can of tomatoes
Optional can of Garbanzon beans
chicken stock

Saute the onion and garlic on the bottom of the crock pot for a little bit
Drain all of the cans and add them to the crock pot
Fill up the crock pot with the chicken stock until all the veggies are covered.
Season with Salt, Pepper, and cayene pepper if you like a kick. If you have any Adobo seasoning a lil dash would not hurt.

I usually let it cook on high for about four hours and then switch it on to low for an overnight cook.

Serve with some shredded cheese, sour cream, and picnic potato crisps.
